newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, China plan to set up joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, China plan to set up joint ventures.

text.p: Visiting Chinese Vice Premier Li Lanqing said on Wednesday his country was interested in establishing industrial joint ventures with Bulgaria.
"We are offering 10 sectors in which we can cooperate in joint ventures," Li told a news conference winding up his four day visit.
The ventures include assembling tractors, bicycles and television sets, and the production of pharmaceutical products, shoes and clothes.

"We are interested in cooperating in the field of telecommunications," Li said, adding that the Chinese delegation had presented Bulgaria with a 2,000-line digital telephone exchange as an example of their modern technology.
Chinese firms are interested in importing Bulgarian equipment for the production of fruit juice, officials said.
Li said Bulgaria and China had the potential to revive their economic and trade ties, which have been neglected since the end of Communist rule in Bulgaria.
Bulgaria hopes to bring current annual trade of less than $50 million back up to its 1990 levels of $130 million.

Bulgaria's biggest fertiliser producer Himko on Monday signed a $30 million deal with China's Xinohem to supply 150,000 tonnes of urea per year. The contract is for a year initially but could be extended, Bulgarian officials said.
Li said the Chinese government would support Bulgaria's interest in coal from China but the firms from both sides should agree terms.
Bulgarian officials have also cited possibilities for cooperation in the fields of banking, insurance and technology.
